blocks.text: Amos opens with a stark divine accusation: God will speak 'against you' Israel, invoking the exodus tradition immediately. The phrase 'the whole family which I brought up out of the land of Egypt' invokes Israel's foundational election moment. However, Amos radically redefines what that election means. The statement 'You only have I known of all the families of the earth' does not confer privilege or immunity; instead, it becomes the very grounds for intensified judgment. Knowledge of Israel by God entails accountability, not protection. Knowing Israel therefore means visiting upon them 'all your iniquities'—their transgressions are now compounded by covenant breach. Amos transforms the exodus narrative from a source of assurance into a basis for divine judgment, establishing the logical foundation for the judgment oracles that follow.
